question_type: Change (percentage points) in a tax source's share of total receipts between two CALENDAR years, built by summing 12 monthly FFO rows per year from the right issues
decisive_step: Refuse the fiscal-year annual rows (stub 'Fiscal year or month') and build each calendar year from 12 monthly rows: FFO-2 col (4) 'Income taxes > Net' (individual) and FFO-1 col (1) total receipts, taking CY2010 from the March 2011 issue and CY2011 from the March 2012 issue (a March issue's 13-month window Dec(Y-1)..Dec(Y) holds one full calendar year), and NOT from the FFO-2 continuation column labelled 'Total (44)', which the parser mislabels (it holds net miscellaneous receipts). Reference: worklog.md Step 3 (lines 17-21), Step 4 line 28 (mislabel), calc.py:13-41 (48 cells asserted against corpus lines), vintage_check.py (only negligible revisions).

At a[41] decided to sum monthly rows; printings --row '2010 - Jan' then '2010-01' (a[46]-[48]) returned the month with every printing and the latest value, so it looped printings over 24 months for FFO-2 'Income taxes > Net' (a[50]-[56]) and FFO-1 'Total receipts' (a[58]), took the latest printing of each, and computed the two shares and their difference with calc (a[60]). 223 s, 62 steps.
a.saw_correct_evidence: yes - all 48 monthly cells printed by printings with issue:line (a[50]-[58]); the printings SUMMARY lines named the March 2011 / March 2012 issues as latest printings

notes: 1) Compared with v8 (none and cards arms wrong on FY-vs-CY and on month rows inheriting the wrong year), all three v9 cells got it: the difference is that printings/show_table now key month rows as YYYY-MM with the year resolved ('2010-01', a[46]) and report the latest printing, so the year-label-inheritance error is gone; cell b had no advice text and was still right, which suggests the tool's explicit period keys matter more than the text sentence. 2) The 8,000-byte page limit is the main friction on 24-month questions: a[52] and c[51] were both cut, forcing re-runs or in-calc subprocess parsing; a range/batch mode for printings is the natural fix. 3) The FFO-2 'Total (44)' mislabel (b[45]-[48]) is a latent trap in every issue 2010-2013; a header identity check would catch it. 4) The 'grounded' gate mis-fired on a Python loop bound (b[56]-[57]); harmless here but it will annoy on every script-style calc. 5) All cells answered '<value> percentage points'; the unit suffix was accepted by the grader.
